errorCodes.meaning: HCP `invalid-token` (HCP 5.5): "Missing, malformed, or expired authorization evidence", here the access token the request presents. A token issued under a revoked grant, a relinquished one included (HCP 5.2.7), fails here too: HCP requires that no request presenting evidence issued under a revoked grant succeeds, but names no error (HCP 6.2.2), and this family reads that evidence as invalid, pending HCP confirmation (question 2). Such a failure is itself a notice of revocation to the client (HCP 6.2.2). Defined once for the family in [the hcp family conventions](/specs/hcp/_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md#1-family-error-codes).

Response.description: The grant is revoked. Carries HCP's `204 No Content`, which has no body, so the payload is the empty object. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.
Response.title: HCP — Revoke Grant — response payload

Urn.description: An HCP identifier: a UUID in `urn:uuid:` form, of any UUID version (HCP 4.2), as HCP uses for entry, grant, directive and retrieval identifiers.

schema.description: The request payload of the HCP 2.0-draft-3 Revoke grant operation (HCP 6.2, 5.4; `DELETE /v2/grants/{grantId}` in HCP 9.2): a Management Client, acting for the Authorizing Principal, ends a grant. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3. Every maxLength, maxItems and maxProperties in this schema is a Trust Tasks framework bound (SPEC §7.3 item 19), not an HCP requirement; so is every minLength or minItems of 1 on a member HCP's own schema allows to be empty.

accessToken.description: The Management Client's HCP access token (HCP 9.3), carried unchanged. HCP's HTTP Binding sends it as a Bearer token; this member carries it in the document. The provider validates it exactly as over HTTP and treats it as opaque. The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement. OPTIONAL: where it is absent, the provider authenticates the request's `issuer` VID, by the REQUIRED request proof, as a Management Client the Authorizing Principal enrolled (HCP 3.2.3), and refuses any other issuer with permissionDenied; where it is present, the token rules apply unchanged. Pending HCP confirmation (question 56).

grantId.description: HCP `grantId` (the `{grantId}` path parameter of HCP 9.2): the grant to revoke.
